public/grant_table.verdict: UNRESOLVED - production is strictly wider than a clean replay
public/grant_table.detail: 24 table/role pairs differ, every one in the same direction. anon holds SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE in production on 13 tables where a clean replay grants none: ai_calls, ai_usage_counters, chat_messages, chat_sessions, command_log, item_inquiries, outfit_calendar, outfit_reactions, style_feedback, style_profiles, tag_corrections, wardrobe_gaps, wishlist_items (52 grants). authenticated holds 18 further grants across 11 tables. 52 + 18 = 70, which closes the count exactly.

public/grant_routine.verdict: UNRESOLVED - production is strictly wider than a clean replay
public/grant_routine.detail: service_role holds EXECUTE on all 102 public functions in production against 11 in a clean replay (91). anon holds EXECUTE on apply_outfit_reaction, claim_command, current_ai_consent_version, log_outfit_wear and plan_outfit_tx (5), and authenticated on log_outfit_wear (1). 91 + 5 + 1 = 97.

schema_comparison.root_cause_of_the_grant_divergence: Supabase PROJECT-CREATION default privileges, which granted anon/authenticated/service_role full rights on every object created in public before 20260805213000 ran `alter default privileges in schema public revoke all on tables from anon, authenticated`. The current Supabase CLI image does not set those defaults, so a fresh replay never receives them. This is the same class of drift 20260806100000_explicit_client_grants.sql and 20260806101000_service_role_grants.sql were written to close for the authenticated-table and service_role-table halves; the anon-table and all-routine halves were never written down. Production's pg_default_acl still shows public/postgres functions as `postgres=X/postgres | service_role=X/postgres`, which is why every function carries service_role EXECUTE there and only the 11 explicitly granted ones do in CI.
schema_comparison.risk_assessment: RLS is enabled on all 13 anon-reachable tables, so a wider GRANT does not by itself expose rows - a policy is still required. The divergence is nonetheless real, app-owned and unwritten-down. The one difference that runs the other way in effect is log_outfit_wear: a database built from this repo would refuse it to authenticated, where production allows it. That function is superseded by wear_outfit_tx and is retained only for old clients.
schema_comparison.resolution_status: NOT RESOLVED IN GATE 3, BY CONSTRUCTION. Closing it means either revoking in production or writing new migrations that grant in CI - both are production or schema changes outside this gate's read-only remit. Carried forward with exact counts and object lists rather than left implicit.
